headline: NCP names mayoral candidates for Dhaka city polls
summary: Nasiruddin Patwary will contest for Dhaka South and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain for Dhaka North, the party announced.
details: The National Citizen Party (NCP) has formally named Nasiruddin Patwary, its Chief Coordinator, as the mayoral candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, its spokesperson, as the candidate for Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC).
The announcement was made by NCP Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam at a coordination meeting with prospective councillor candidates at the party's Banglamotor office in Dhaka.

Nahid Islam provided organizational directives on election preparations and the party's political activities in the capital, urging leaders to map local civic problems and build campaigns around resident issues.
Party leaders were also instructed to maintain regular contact with the families of those killed and injured during the July Uprising and provide them with support.
Nasiruddin Patwary stated that the NCP will contest local government elections across the country independently, though it will maintain political coordination with its 11-party alliance partners.
The party has already announced candidates for approximately 100 upazila and municipality posts and expects to declare more than 100 additional nominations within the next few days.
caption:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has officially named its mayoral candidates for the Dhaka city polls.

The National Citizen Party (NCP) has formally named Nasiruddin Patwary, its Chief Coordinator, as the mayoral candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, its spokesperson, as the candidate for Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC).

The announcement was made by NCP Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam at a coordination meeting with prospective councillor candidates at the party's Banglamotor office in Dhaka.

Nahid Islam provided organizational directives on election preparations and the party's political activities in the capital, urging leaders to map local civic problems and build campaigns around resident issues.

Party leaders were also instructed to maintain regular contact with the families of those killed and injured during the July Uprising and provide them with support.

Nasiruddin Patwary stated that the NCP will contest local government elections across the country independently, though it will maintain political coordination with its 11-party alliance partners.

The party has already announced candidates for approximately 100 upazila and municipality posts and expects to declare more than 100 additional nominations within the next few days.

headline_marked: Tk 11,000 crore claim: [[Asif Mahmud denies money laundering]] allegations
headline: Tk 11,000 crore claim: Asif Mahmud denies money laundering allegations
summary: The National Citizen Party spokesperson rejects claims of laundering funds to Australia, Dubai, and Singapore, calling the ACC probe 'politically motivated'.
details: National Citizen Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has rejected allegations that he laundered approximately Tk 11,000 crore to destinations including Australia, Dubai, and Singapore.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) announced it is investigating claims of corruption and irregularities regarding recruitment, transfers, and promotions at the Ministry of Youth and Sports during Asif's tenure as an adviser.
At a press conference in Banglamotor, Asif termed the inquiry 'politically motivated' and claimed that some of the decisions cited in the allegations were made after he had left office.
He further alleged that the ACC is being used as a 'weapon' following the scrapping of an ordinance intended to reform the commission.
During the event, Asif also criticized the current government's economic and energy policies, accusing it of failing to deliver on its employment promises.
He claimed the BNP had promised one crore jobs but instead 'opened up avenues for extortion,' alleging that employment was created for 50 lakh party members.
Asif also expressed concern over public processions by the banned Awami League, describing them as a threat to public safety, particularly in Dhaka-17.
NCP Chief Coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary added that the party has decided to contest the upcoming local government elections independently.
caption:
Tk 11,000 crore laundering claim. Asif Mahmud hits back, calling the ACC probe 'politically motivated'.

National Citizen Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has rejected allegations that he laundered approximately Tk 11,000 crore to destinations including Australia, Dubai, and Singapore.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) announced it is investigating claims of corruption and irregularities regarding recruitment, transfers, and promotions at the Ministry of Youth and Sports during Asif's tenure as an adviser.

At a press conference in Banglamotor, Asif termed the inquiry 'politically motivated' and claimed that some of the decisions cited in the allegations were made after he had left office.

He further alleged that the ACC is being used as a 'weapon' following the scrapping of an ordinance intended to reform the commission.

During the event, Asif also criticized the current government's economic and energy policies, accusing it of failing to deliver on its employment promises.

He claimed the BNP had promised one crore jobs but instead 'opened up avenues for extortion,' alleging that employment was created for 50 lakh party members.

Asif also expressed concern over public processions by the banned Awami League, describing them as a threat to public safety, particularly in Dhaka-17.

NCP Chief Coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary added that the party has decided to contest the upcoming local government elections independently.
